Even a simple installation of airbyte on my local machine fails :( I tried docker-compose up! ... this feedback will sound harsh but companies are taking words 'open source' for a complete ride.

I had a read through your docs but was unable to find any info on how you handle the sync of hard deletions from sources... In incremental mode, for common DBs e.g. MySQL/Postgres, will Airbyte pick up hard deletions ever?

Airbyte is a godsend for us. It works really well for most use cases. Unfortunately, we had to write our custom thing for a large table (8 billion rows) and 'tricked' Airbyte into thinking it had done the first sync. After that, it continued to sync happily.
For me right now, Airbyte is that tool I wish we had at my last startup. We were pulling data from a lot of weird places... Would've loved to have someone else take care of all that for us.

I've been using Stitch Data for a couple of years and I've find myself 'fighting' with their support team about bugs I think were Singer related, mainly with DDL commands (contrasting with Airbyte's own protocol choice).
Just to clarify, this is not a fully open source project. More like freemium... If you want security, you have to pay. There are non-free parts to it that you are not allowed to use.
(We use airbyte at my company, although we self-host it.) ...you're very well-positioned for this opportunity than most people realize, given your reputable brand and your uncanny expertise in etl.
Congrats, you built an ETL pipeline and called it an agent. The industry has come full circle.

We originally wanted to use the airbyte white-label platform, but the team said that it was being deprecated... I think this really drives home just how crucial it is to have a clear model for accessing your data, and Airbyte has been great at that for quite a while.
